ozzie-firstsale.title: Oral History of Raymond (Ray) Ozzie (CHM Reference number X9392.2021)
ozzie-firstsale.author: Ray Ozzie, interviewed by Marc Weber
ozzie-firstsale.quote: We launched and our first sale was on December 7th of ’89; it was five years to the day after we had-- I had spun out of-- I signed my contract with Lotus.
supports: Notes' first sale, December 7th 1989 - stated by Ozzie in a 2020 recorded interview, i.e. a recollection 31 years later, not a shipping record
Five years to the day earlier, December 7th 1984, Ozzie signed his contract with Lotus — he says 'contract', not 'founded'

ozzie-funding.title: Oral History of Raymond (Ray) Ozzie (CHM Reference number X9392.2021)
ozzie-funding.author: Ray Ozzie, interviewed by Marc Weber
ozzie-funding.quote: They funded us with an initial check of 1.2 million, but it was an option to purchase rights to the product at a future time if they would be willing to commit to marketing it with the full power of their marketing organization.
supports: Lotus funded Iris Associates with an initial cheque of $1.2 million and held only an option, no equity
A widely repeated $1.3 million figure appears in secondary summaries; the primary source says 1.2 million
Same passage dates the cheque: 'December 7th, ’84, I called my-- Tim Halvorsen and Len Kawell ... I said, “I got the check; let’s go,” and they quit their jobs and they joined me in January'

ozzie-beckhardt.title: Oral History of Raymond (Ray) Ozzie (CHM Reference number X9392.2021)
ozzie-beckhardt.author: Ray Ozzie, interviewed by Marc Weber
ozzie-beckhardt.quote: It was very clear maybe six months on that in order to make it operate in a distributed manner we needed to take the concept of synchronization and replication much more seriously, so we hired another guy, Steve Beckhardt, who dealt with the replication of the NoSQL database that I had done.
supports: Replication was recognised as a separate, specialist problem about six months into the build and staffed with a dedicated hire

Elsewhere in the same transcript: 'there would be no Lotus Notes without Tim Halvorsen, Len Kawell and I, and also Steven Beckhardt, who did the replication, and Alan Eldridge, who was on the security side.' The transcript spells the name both Steve and Steven.

ozzie-dialup.title: Oral History of Raymond (Ray) Ozzie (CHM Reference number X9392.2021)
ozzie-dialup.author: Ray Ozzie, interviewed by Marc Weber
ozzie-dialup.quote: One server would use dial- up-- telephones to dial up— Weber: Store and forward. Ozzie: --another one and do store and forward and that-- because there was no Internet that was the way things that-- the way things worked
supports: Notes replication was modelled on UUCP-style dial-up store-and-forward because there was no ubiquitous internet to build on
The hyphen inside 'dial- up' is a line break in the CHM transcript PDF, reproduced as printed

domino-conflict.title: Replication or save conflicts — HCL Domino 10.0.1 Administrator help
domino-conflict.author: HCL Software (originally IBM Domino Administrator Help)
domino-conflict.quote: These response documents have the title Replication or Save Conflict.
supports: The losing copy is preserved as a response document, i.e. a child of the surviving main document, not a sibling

Same page: 'Domino uses the $Revisions field, which tracks the date and time of each document editing session, to determine which document becomes the main document and which documents become responses.'
Same page: 'Multiple users can simultaneously edit the same document in one copy of a database or edit the same document in different replicas between replication sessions.'
Same page: 'ACL and design changes never result in replication or save conflicts; the most recent change always prevails.'
Page banner reads 'IBM Domino 10.0.1 Administrator Help', not HCL; the domain and the current publisher are HCL, which is why the title and author fields carry both

domino-parent.title: Replication and save conflicts — HCL Domino Designer 12 documentation
domino-parent.author: HCL Software
domino-parent.quote: The document edited and saved the most times becomes the main document; other documents become Replication or Save Conflict documents.
supports: The surviving parent is chosen by number of save operations, not by wall-clock recency
Same page, tie-break: 'the document saved most recently becomes the main document, and the others become Replication or Save Conflict documents.'
Same page, save conflicts on a single replica: 'the first document saved becomes the main document'
Page banner reads 'HCL Domino Designer 12.0.1 documentation'; the URL path is 12.0.0

domino-merge.title: Replication and save conflicts — HCL Domino Designer 12 documentation (Merge replication conflicts form property)
domino-merge.author: HCL Software
domino-merge.quote: automatically merge conflicts into one document if no fields conflict
supports: The field-level merge option resolves conflicts only when the two edits touched different fields; two edits to the same field still produce a conflict document
The property applies to replication conflicts, not save conflicts
Page banner reads 'HCL Domino Designer 12.0.1 documentation'; the URL path is 12.0.0

dropbox-conflicted.title: What's a conflicted copy? — Dropbox Help Center
dropbox-conflicted.author: Dropbox
dropbox-conflicted.quote: The editor's username, "conflicted copy", and the save date will be added to the filename.
supports: Dropbox files the losing edit as a peer file whose own name says who made it and when
Same page: 'A conflicted copy is a file that Dropbox creates when multiple people edit the same file at the same time.'
Page states 'Updated May 15, 2025'; the quoted sentence uses curly quotes in the original

unverified: That the conflict mechanism existed in 1989. Nothing in the ledger dates $Revisions, the Replication or Save Conflict response document, or the merge property to Notes 1.0: the CHM oral history never mentions conflicts, merging or revisions at all (checked by full-text search of the transcript), and the only sources are HCL help pages from 2018 and 2021. The prose therefore describes the mechanism in the present tense and attributes it to the Domino help, and card c2 carries 2018, not 1989.

That $Revisions is what detects a replication conflict. Both help pages say only that Domino uses it 'to determine which document becomes the main document and which documents become responses' — winner selection, not detection. The pages define the conflict itself structurally ('two or more users edit the same document and save the changes in different replicas between replications'), so the prose now attributes detection to that definition and gives $Revisions only the winner-naming job the source gives it.
When the 'Merge replication conflicts' form property was introduced. The help pages carry no version history, so 'later releases offered to merge' was removed from the prose.

How long replicas stayed apart between dial-up sessions. 'Replicas drifted for days' was an invented duration and is gone; 'drifted between calls' is what store-and-forward entails. The seam line's 'a phone line that connects at night' was an invented cadence and is also gone.
The price IBM paid for Lotus in 1995. Secondary summaries give $3.2B and $3.5B; no primary filing was opened, so no figure appears in the prose or on a card.

The $1.8B IBM-to-HCL sale of Notes/Domino announced December 2018. Only reachable through secondary encyclopaedia text here; the IBM and HCL press releases both failed to fetch, so it is left out of the prose.

Ozzie's 'roughly 125 million users' by 1997. It is his own hedged recall, offered in answer to the interviewer's leading 'over a hundred million, something like that', and it is not corroborated. Not used.

The exact date Steve Beckhardt joined Iris Associates. Ozzie says only 'maybe six months on' from a January 1985 start, so 1985 is an inference from a hedge. He is the fourth engineer, not 'the fourth hire' — Halvorsen and Kawell joined as partners, Beckhardt is the one Ozzie describes as hired.

Whether Replication or Save Conflict documents were routinely invisible in default views, and any count of how many accumulated unresolved in real deployments. The response-document structure is documented; the claim that users therefore never saw them is not, and it is not asserted anywhere in the prose or the cards.
Iris Associates' office location in 1989. Secondary sources say Westford, Massachusetts; the box-tag uses the organisation and year instead.

That the internet did not exist when Notes replication was designed. Ozzie says 'because there was no Internet that was the way things worked' and immediately corrects himself to 'or that wasn't ubiquitous in a-- commercially'. The prose therefore says there was no internet to lean on, not that there was none.
